name: NACW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The promotion's top singles title, changing hands three times across its own surviving 1999 record, twice by pinfall and once by an interference-marred Royal Rumble.

name: NACW United States Championship
epitaph: A frequently-contested singles title that changed hands three times in five months, ending its own surviving record around the waist of a rising young star.

name: NACW World Television Championship
epitaph: The promotion's midcard singles title, which changed hands four times across its own surviving record, once by a forfeit after a champion's real-world arrest.

name: NACW World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A tag title decided in a four-way match at the promotion's own debut pay-per-view and contested by shifting duos through its own surviving record.

name: NACW Light Heavyweight Championship of the World
epitaph: A title that changed hands four times across the promotion's own surviving record, once inside two minutes and once handed over outright before a match could begin.

name: NACW Toughman Championship
epitaph: A hardcore-styled title defended on a burning scaffold at the promotion's own second World Tour pay-per-view, its own record ending with the belt itself stolen from the winner.
